pr.title: Plan one header for each stack: its project or a title
pr.head: c18541f1d2b825a8a3f2f06c59ac991ca45a2897

summary: Projector's site has a Reviews index that lists every pull request with a published summary, and each summary page has a sidebar that lists the pull requests in its stack, the chain of pull requests where each one's base branch is the head branch of the one beneath it. Neither place says what a stack as a whole is for. Today the only hint is a set of project links that the build derives from each pull request's diff: every project whose folder holds a changed file. That rule links a rename across plans to unrelated projects and links the upper layers of a stack, which implement a plan without editing it, to nothing.

This pull request adds one new plan, docs/projects/stack-header/readme.md, at status: ready and priority: next. It changes no code. The plan is written against main as #215 left it: the Reviews index has three columns (pull request, status, updated), no Projects column, and Open and Closed boxes. The plan gives every stack, a pull request alone included, exactly one header: the project the stack carries out, linked to the project's page, or a short plain-text title when it has none.

1. A summary records its project. summary.json gains a project field, and name becomes the stack's title. init writes null, which means undecided, and publish refuses it, so every new summary states a choice.
  2. The build picks one header per stack. It walks the stack's layers from the bottom up and takes the first project the site has a page for. Without one, it takes the first non-empty name, and without that, the bottom pull request's title.
  3. The index and the sidebar draw it. A header row opens each stack on the Reviews index, and one header replaces the sidebar's project rows. The Projects column goes.
  4. Older summaries get a header without republishing. A summary with no project keeps today's answer where today's answer is a single project, and otherwise gets its title.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Stack: pull requests chained by base branch, listed bottom layer first.
  • Layer: one pull request in a stack.
  • Header: the one line drawn above a stack, a project link or a title.
  • Summaries ref: refs/projector/summaries, the hidden ref the site builds summaries from.
  • Migration rule: how the build chooses a project for a summary published before the project field existed.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• First head. One finding. Step 3 of § 2.1 told each upper layer to copy the project of the layer beneath it whenever it was set. Because "" counts as set, a stack that opens with a refactor would have lost its project in every layer above.
  • This head. The plan fixes the finding: step 3 copies only a non-empty project and name. It also says how an update sets project on a summary published before the field existed, and it rewrites the index sections for the code that #215 merged. Review verdict: clean.

groups.title: The stack header plan
groups.kicker: One header per stack, chosen from the summaries' recorded project or title.
intro: The whole pull request is this one plan. Read it in order: § 1 is the problem, § 2 the design, § 3 the reasons, § 4 the tests the implementation must add, and § 6 how it meets the open #215.

The design has two halves. The summarizing agent decides the project, in the summarize-pr skill (§ 2.1). The site build only checks that decision and picks one answer per stack, from the lowest layer up (§ 2.2). Keep those halves apart when you read: the build's rule tolerates layers that disagree, but the skill's steps decide what the layers record in the first place.

files.note: The new plan: the problem, the data, the build's rule, the drawing, the tests, and the rollout.

checks.text: § 1 describes today's rule. project_linker in src/projector/site/__init__.py returns every project whose folder holds a changed file, after any names in the summary's undocumented projects list. After #215 those links reach only the sidebar and the project pages, not the index.
null and "" mean different things. null means nobody chose, and publish refuses it. "" means this pull request names no project, and a layer above it can still give the stack one.

Step 3 copies the beneath layer's project only when it is a non-empty string, and its name only when it is non-empty. A stack that opens with a refactor recording "" keeps the project a layer above it records. The review checked this against the "" row of the table, § 2.2 step 3, and § 3.

review-pr updates an existing summary rather than starting over. Every summary published before this change lacks project, so the update path has to set it, or the first republish of each open pull request would be refused.

The build already computes stack_groups for the Reviews index, but today it writes each page before it computes the groups. Step 1 means the implementation has to reorder build_summaries so the header is known before any page is written, as § 2.5 says.

This is the migration rule for summaries published before the field. The review counted the summaries on the ref: none records projects, so in practice the diff decides, and only a diff that touches exactly one project's files keeps a project.

site.css on main pads each body's first row with table.tbl.reviews tbody tr:first-child td { padding-top: 6px; }. The review confirmed that the rule exists and that the header row, a th, would displace it. This paragraph moves the padding to the header.
validate in src/projector/summary.py requires pr.title, and both build_summaries and project site page run it, so dropping the name fallback from pr_title changes no page.
